dedupe_keys.name: omses de optimal mine site energy supply design envelope model

description: OMSES_DE is a small optimisation model for sizing the energy supply of a remote mine site, published with the input demand data of Jeff Eastick's MASc thesis "Optimization of Small Modular Nuclear Reactor Integration at a Remote Mine Site in Canada" at Laurentian University. The Borealis dataset page lists the model program OMSES_DE.py, a plotting program OPlots.py, a main.py driver, a blank input table and a model input table, a README and a licence file, and says the programs are used with the Gurobi solver. It was deposited on 21 December 2020 and released on 8 February 2021 as version 1, with every file downloadable and the dataset free under CC0 1.0; the page says the code is mirrored to a GitHub repository (jeastick/OMSES) for later work. Coverage is one generic remote Canadian mine site. Caveats: Gurobi is a commercial solver, the demand data describe one thesis case, not measured site loads, and validation and the exact technologies in the supply mix are not stated on the page read. For simulation it gives a worked optimisation of off-grid power and heat supply for mines, useful for testing how remote extraction sites ride through fuel supply disruption and for comparing diesel, renewables, storage and small modular reactors. Related catalogue records include Mapping Mining Areas in the Tropics, the WAPHA global metal mines database and the Energy and Industry Facilities Composite.
